action: Audited global.json (SDK 11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103), Directory.Packages.props, and all four csproj files. Found ProjectName.Runtime.csproj referenced <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Ollama" /> pinned via CPM to Version 9.7.0-preview.1.25356.2 -- roughly a year behind the rest of the stack (Microsoft.Agents.AI 1.20.0, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience/ServiceDiscovery 10.9.0, Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi 11.0.0-preview.7). Confirmed via read of ProjectName.Runtime/Program.cs that no code anywhere actually uses the Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Ollama namespace -- the real Ollama wiring is builder.AddOllamaApiClient(...) from CommunityToolkit.Aspire.OllamaSharp 13.5.1-beta.736. This stale, unused, badly-mismatched package pin is the most plausible source of the IDE showing Ollama-related symbols as unknown (NuGet version-conflict/downgrade noise confusing the language service) even though a from-scratch dotnet build can still succeed. Removed the dead <PackageVersion> entry from Directory.Packages.props and the dead <PackageReference> from ProjectName.Runtime.csproj (with an explanatory comment left in Directory.Packages.props citing this trail). Re-ran 'dotnet build .\ProjectName.slnx -m:1' after the change: Build succeeded, 0 Error(s). Also separately observed an unrelated one-off build failure (MSB3027/MSB3021 file-lock on ProjectName.ServiceDefaults.dll) on the very first parallel build attempt right after ProjectName.OrchestrationApi was added to the solution; this is a known transient MSBuild parallel-copy race on a freshly-added project with no incremental cache yet, not a real code error -- it did not recur on rebuild and is not part of the Ollama complaint. Did not touch ProjectName.AppHost/AppHost.cs, ProjectName.OrchestrationApi, or any other file with the user's own pending edits; only edited the two files needed for this specific fix, and left both edits uncommitted (out of git add scope) since both files already carry unrelated in-progress changes from the user's own live editing session -- committing them would mix authorship into the user's WIP.

Fetched https://aspire.dev/get-started/aspire-mcp-server/ (current, non-cached) and confirmed the Aspire MCP server is a real, current (2026) Aspire CLI feature: started via 'aspire agent mcp' (bootstrapped/configured via 'aspire agent init', which generates client config for VS Code / Claude Code / Copilot CLI / OpenCode). Transport is STDIO (a local child process, no open network ports -- only the parent AI-assistant process that spawned it can talk to it), so no auth is needed. It exposes 14 tools: list_resources, list_apphosts, select_apphost, list_console_logs, list_structured_logs, list_traces, execute_resource_command, list_docs, search_docs, get_doc, get_integration_docs, doctor, refresh_tools -- giving resource metadata (names/types/states/health/endpoints) and telemetry (console logs, structured logs, distributed traces), explicitly excluding source code, secrets, and env vars. The former /get-started/configure-mcp/ page now redirects to /get-started/ai-coding-agents/, which states the server 'uses the STDIO transport protocol and may work with other agentic coding environments that support this MCP communication protocol' beyond the four officially wired ones -- i.e. it is not locked to those four clients; any MCP-capable client (including this repo's own PMCR-O agent-skill runtime) can in principle add it as an MCP server by spawning 'aspire agent mcp' as a subprocess from a working directory where an AppHost project (or aspire.config.json, which ProjectName.AppHost already has, pointing at ProjectName.AppHost.csproj) can be resolved. Recommendation for the requested .NET Aspire agent-skill plugin (out of scope to build in this spike): a new plugins/pmcro-aspire skill whose scripts shell out to 'aspire agent mcp' / use its 14 tools to answer questions like 'is the runtime resource healthy' or 'show me the last traces' from within a PMCR-O cycle, rather than reimplementing Aspire resource introspection from scratch. Filing this as a next_seed for the planner role.
